newsitem.title: CANADA: Seattle magnate buys out Vancouver Grizzlies, Canucks.
newsitem.headline: Seattle magnate buys out Vancouver Grizzlies, Canucks.

text.p: Seattle tycoon John McCaw became the sole owner of the company that controls Vancouver's hockey club and owns its basketball franchise and downtown sports arena in a deal announced Tuesday.
McCaw, who bought the majority of Orca Bay Sports and Entertainment last year, announced he was buying the remaining shares held by minority owner Arthur Griffiths.
"I love sports. I love Vancouver," McCaw said when asked his reasons for the deal. "The fact that we (Seattle and Vancouver) are separated by a border means little to me."

Orca Bay owns a new downtown sports arena called GM Place and the Vancouver Grizzlies National Basketball Association team. It also owns 72 percent with the right to acquire an additional 14 percent of Northwest Sprts Enterprises Ltd., which owns the Vancouver Canucks hockey team.
Neither man would reveal the size of the stake sold Tuesday or the amount paid. Sports sources said they believed McCaw already owned around 90 percent of the Orca Bay.
Griffiths said Tuesday he asked a reluctant McCaw to buy him out for personal and financial reasons.

McCaw, who also owns part of Seattle's Mariners baseball team, is one of four brothers who founded McCaw Cellular Communications, which was sold to AT&T Corp. in 1994. Forbes magazine last month estimated his fortune at $750 million.
Publicity-shy in the extreme, McCaw refused to be photographed or appear at a news conference Tuesday. Instead, he met reporters two at a time for a few brief questions.
McCaw said he would focus on building Orca Bay's current operations but ultimately might consider expansion options, including adding properties such as a National Football League team.
"Dollars are needed to build this company," he said.
Griffiths has said he was financially drained by efforts to build the C$160 million ($120 million) GM Place and back a deal to gain an NBA team in 1994.
Griffiths' late father founded the Canucks. The family also has interests in television and radio broadcasting.
